summary: Rungs M1->M2, M2->M3, M3->M4 and M4->M5 (and M5->M6, known) never re-read user_version under the write lock and then stamp a lower PRAGMA user_version unconditionally, so a stale opener downgrades a store another opener already climbed to v9 and leaves it permanently refused.
failure_scenario: Opener B reads user_version=4 (or 5, 3, 2, or 0 with legacy runs) before the lock; opener A climbs the store to 9 and commits; B then runs _migrate_m4_to_m5 (BEGIN IMMEDIATE followed by executescript, which commits and drops the lock; the PRAGMA user_version=5 then runs in autocommit with no recheck) or _migrate_m2_to_m3 (no BEGIN, no recheck), setting user_version back to 5/3/2. B then continues up the ladder; M6->M7 and M7->M8 recheck and B's chain ends with 'schema 7 already carries current capability accounting structure' JournalDamaged. The store is left at user_version 7 (or 2-6 if B dies) with v9 tables and every later open raises JournalDamaged (ADR 0016 forbids heal-on-open). M1->M2 additionally re-runs the non-idempotent inputs_json/next_event_seq backfill over live rows, and M3->M4 rewrites live capability_lease rows. Only M6->M7, M7->M8 and M8->M9 carry the under-lock re-read.
evidence: Executed. (a) Called each stale step directly on a healthy v9 store: m2_to_m3 left version 3, m3_to_m4 version 4, m4_to_m5 version 5, m5_to_m6 version 6, m1_to_m2 version 2; every store except m1 was then refused on reopen with 'schema 7 already carries current capability accounting structure' (m1 not re-opened). (b) Through the public SqliteJournal(path) constructor, with only the first PRAGMA user_version read of the loser faked to 4 (then 5) to model the stale pre-lock read: constructor raised JournalDamaged, user_version ended at 7, a later plain SqliteJournal(path) raised the same JournalDamaged. Scripts in scratchpad race.py and race2.py. The v9 version-rung race in the brief (M5->M6) is the same root; this finding extends it to four more rungs, which a fix scoped to M5->M6 would leave open. Pre-existing.

summary: The migration-race tests exercise only the M6->M7 re-check and the fresh create, by calling private step functions directly on an already-current store, so they pass without ever running the constructor ladder under concurrency and cannot see the un-guarded M1-M5 rungs.
failure_scenario: The loser test calls loser._migrate_m6_to_m7(connection) on a v9 store; it only proves the != 6 guard returns. No test opens through SqliteJournal(path) with a stale version, no test covers M1->M2..M5->M6 or M7->M8/M8->M9 stale openers, so deleting the guards on any other rung, or the downgrade in finding 1, stays green.
evidence: Read the file; the only rung call is _migrate_m6_to_m7. Wrote race2.py to show the public-constructor route reproduces the failure that these tests do not detect. Test gap, introduced with the race tests.

summary: _migrate_m4_to_m5 and _migrate_m5_to_m6 run 'BEGIN IMMEDIATE' and then executescript(), which implicitly COMMITs and releases the write lock, so neither rung is atomic with its version stamp and the lock they appear to take protects nothing.
failure_scenario: Process dies (or another opener interleaves) between executescript(_V5_SCHEMA/_V6_SCHEMA) and 'PRAGMA user_version = N': the tables exist at the old version; the lock was already released so a concurrent opener can enter the same rung. Idempotent CREATE IF NOT EXISTS makes a crash-only retry benign, but the interleaving is exactly what lets finding 1 downgrade the store.
evidence: Source read: Python sqlite3 executescript commits any pending transaction first (the repo's own _ddl_statements docstring at line 283 states this); the same file uses _ddl_statements to avoid it only in the fresh create. Not separately executed; partially covered by finding 1 run.

summary: RunHost._scan_answered_waits / parked_waits / answered_requests: wake eligibility derives from the stored reply and the PARKED+RunParked fence (status and next_event_seq in one snapshot, repeated by _fill_capacity via max_event_seq), not from command completion, so a reply committed before its command completes still wakes the run; the cut persists across ticks and restarts from the beginning each cycle so late-parked runs are seen.

Command ownership: claim_command bumps owner_epoch on expiry, _command_fenced and _terminal_command require state=prepared and owner/epoch match, rejection is refused when a domain fact owned by the command exists (_domain_fact_owned_by), and committed resume intents are rebuilt from plan+terminal response by _resume_intent_from_record (rejected -> None), so a stale owner cannot complete or reject over a reclaimed command; the runs_resume launch is process-local but fenced by the baseline event sequence and AttemptCause, so duplicate launches cannot attempt twice. Did not trace _sqlite_channels reply recovery or channel crash-seam tests in depth; not claimed sound.
M6->M7, M7->M8 and M8->M9 re-read user_version under BEGIN IMMEDIATE and roll back when it moved; the fresh-create path re-reads under the lock and publishes tables and version in one transaction.
